packet.component_identity_contract: Return stance_components as one array. Each array item is one atomic component object whose object kind, object interpretation, expression kind, and one source alias belong together. Never return parallel component columns and never combine two source aliases in one component.
packet.endpoint_definition: Compare the later working answer with what still limits or could reopen it.
packet.expression_interpretation_contract: Classify force from the source speaker's relation to the component. Reserve reported_without_endorsement for attributing a stance to someone else. Preserve the speaker's own desire, counterpressure, uncertainty, leaning, commitment, and conditional willingness without flattening or upgrading them.

focal_region.annotated_sentence_text:
[Turn 1 USER]
e001	My mother is seventy-nine and lives alone four hours from me.
e002	She fell recently.
e003	It did not cause a serious injury, but it frightened all of us enough that my brother and I immediately started discussing whether she should move closer to one of us.
e004	She has lived in the same apartment for years, knows her neighbors, sees friends nearby, and is attached to ordinary routines that sound small until you imagine losing all of them at once.
e005	Repairs and appointments are becoming harder.
e006	Some days she says moving would be a relief.
e007	Other days she says we are using one frightening event to take over her life.
e008	My brother thinks waiting is denial.
e009	I think planning before a crisis is responsible, but I also see how a family can call something planning after it has already decided which answer counts as safe.
e010	I want to help without turning our fear into a decision she did not make.
[Turn 1 ASSISTANT]
e011	Separate immediate support from a permanent move, and keep your mother's authority central.
e012	Compare real local support with real nearby options, including what each sibling can sustain.
e013	The fall matters, but it cannot represent her whole life or decide for her.
[Turn 2 USER]
e014	My brother thinks we are avoiding reality.
e015	He has two young children and cannot travel often, while I work remotely and have taken most of the calls.
e016	I am resentful that “closer to family” may mean closer to me and more work for me.
e017	At the same time, I do not want my resentment to become an argument for leaving her without enough help.
e018	My mother notices the tension and sometimes says she will move just to stop us arguing.
[Turn 2 ASSISTANT]
e019	Her offer to end the conflict is not the same as a settled preference.
e020	Make the care contributions explicit before presenting either location as a family solution.
e021	Include time, travel, administration, emergencies, and money, and ask what each of you can sustain.
e022	A plan that depends on your unspoken availability is neither fair to you nor reliable for her.
[Turn 3 USER]
e023	We did look locally.
e024	A neighbor can check in, there is cleaning and transport, and the building may replace the bathtub.
e025	I called her distrust of services resistance.
e026	She reminded me one company already cancelled twice.
e027	That was unfair of me; her skepticism has evidence.
[Turn 3 ASSISTANT]
e028	Then reliability and trust are part of the option, not obstacles to it.
e029	Ask providers about continuity, backup, scheduling, and a gradual introduction.
e030	Your mother can choose which supports to try and who is present initially.
e031	Compare the actual local package with the actual nearby-housing option rather than an ideal service network with an unspecified move.
[Turn 4 USER]
e032	There is an apartment complex near me with independent units and optional support, but we have only read its brochure.
e033	The waiting list may be six months.
e034	My mother has not visited and says she will not tour a place if we are going to treat the visit as consent.
e035	I said a tour is just information, and she replied that families often call something information after they have already decided what it means.
[Turn 4 ASSISTANT]
e036	Agree in advance what the visit does and does not decide.
e037	She might tour it to learn what she likes or rejects, with no application that day and no family meeting immediately afterward.
e038	Also visit the ordinary neighborhood and consider how she would maintain friendships and travel back.
e039	Information gathering is more credible when the process protects her from momentum.
[Turn 5 USER]
e040	My brother proposed that she stay with me for a month as a trial.
e041	That sounds practical, but my house has stairs and no private sitting room, so it would test living in my house rather than living nearby.
e042	I also worry that if she gives up local services for the month, returning home will feel like failure.
e043	A short visit could still tell us something about daily contact and whether she likes the area.
[Turn 5 ASSISTANT]
e044	A shorter visit, with her home and local services left intact, can answer whether she likes the area and daily proximity.
e045	If possible, include time in an independent rental rather than only your house.
e046	It will not simulate the proposed apartment or prove long-term care capacity, but it gives you information without requiring a move.
[Turn 6 USER]
e047	You are making this sound much more orderly than it is.
e048	My mother changes the subject when money comes up.
e049	My brother wants a deadline.
e050	And I have not told either of them that I may take a job requiring travel next year.
e051	I do not even know whether I will be offered it.
e052	Still, “move near me” currently includes availability I may not have, and I have allowed everyone to plan around that because admitting uncertainty makes me feel unreliable.
[Turn 6 ASSISTANT]
e053	You are right; I turned a family negotiation into a tidy information plan.
e054	The job possibility is material even while uncertain.
e055	Share it as a scenario, then ask what your mother authorizes you to learn and what each sibling can actually commit under both versions.
e056	A move cannot be built on availability you have not promised.
[Turn 7 USER]
e057	I am not ready to recommend a move.
e058	I will tell them about the possible travel, ask my mother whether she wants a no-commitment visit to the nearby complex, and help her test one local transport service and the shower modification.
e059	My brother and I need to write down what support we can each provide before we ask her to choose around assumptions.
e060	We still do not know the real cost or availability of the nearby option, and I do not know what my mother will prefer after she has seen it.
[Turn 7 ASSISTANT]
e061	Pausing the relocation decision is not avoiding care; it protects the decision from missing inputs and disguised commitments.
e062	The local changes address current friction while the visit, costs, availability, and sibling commitments make the alternatives real enough for your mother to judge.
e063	Preserve her ability to say no after gathering information, and revisit the choice when those facts and her experience exist rather than forcing a direction from today's anxiety.
[Turn 8 USER]
e064	She agreed to visit after making us write down that there would be no application meeting that day.
e065	She liked the apartment more than she expected and loved that she could walk to a café.
e066	She disliked the organized resident activities and said the place felt like joining a life designed by someone else.
e067	Three days in my house exhausted both of us; she was visibly relieved to go home.
e068	Then, halfway back, she asked how long the waiting list was and immediately said, “Do not interpret that question.” That sentence is almost the whole problem.
e069	She is curious.
e070	She is also monitoring us for momentum.
e071	I can answer the factual question, but every action around it now carries meaning for my brother and me that she has explicitly not authorized.
[Turn 8 ASSISTANT]
e072	Treat the visit as mixed evidence exactly as she presented it.
e073	She learned that proximity and the apartment have appeal, while the social environment and your house do not automatically feel like home.
e074	You can answer the waiting-list question without making it a preference.
e075	Ask what she would want to explore next and what parts of her current life would need a credible counterpart before moving became attractive.
[Turn 9 USER]
e076	We obtained the actual costs.
e077	She could afford the nearby apartment if she sold her current one, but keeping both for more than a short overlap would strain her savings.
e078	The waiting list requires a refundable deposit and does not obligate her to accept the first opening.
e079	My brother thinks joining it preserves an option.
e080	My mother says deposits have a way of making families behave as if a decision has been made.
[Turn 9 ASSISTANT]
e081	The deposit is financially reversible but can create social momentum.
e082	If she chooses to join, document that she controls acceptance, can withdraw without justification, and will review the choice only when a real unit is offered.
e083	Keep local improvements moving so the waiting list is not framed as the only responsible path.
e084	Her concern is about process pressure, not a misunderstanding of refundability.
[Turn 10 USER]
e085	The possible travel has become real.
e086	I was offered the job, with one week away most months.
e087	I have not accepted it.
e088	My brother can handle bills and appointments remotely but cannot promise emergency visits.
e089	He offered to contribute to paid local support if our mother stays.
e090	I feel guilty that my career decision changes the apparent safety of her options, and I also resist making my job conditional on living near her after she may choose not to move.
[Turn 10 ASSISTANT]
e091	Do not let either decision silently decide the other.
e092	Show the support plan under both job outcomes.
e093	Your work is a condition to plan around, not a moral test; her move cannot rely on availability you did not promise.
[Turn 11 USER]
e094	The transport service and shower change are working better than she expected.
e095	That matters because “stay” is now a little more real and not just the absence of moving.
e096	She still worries about repairs and about being alone after another fall.
e097	She wants to join the nearby waiting list while continuing to live at home.
e098	My brother calls this the obvious compromise: preserve the option, solve today's problems, decide later.
e099	I think it may be sensible.
e100	I also hear how quickly “join the list” becomes the first step of a plan she did not say she had.
e101	We still do not have a reliable local emergency contact.
e102	She is still divided about leaving friends.
e103	A refundable deposit can preserve financial choice and still create a family narrative that makes saying no harder when a unit finally appears.
[Turn 11 ASSISTANT]
e104	Joining the list can preserve a future choice while current support is strengthened, but it does not resolve the current vulnerability.
e105	Build the local emergency and repair plan now, with your mother's agreement, and review how the new services perform.
e106	Define the waiting-list decision as permission to receive an offer, not a commitment to move.
e107	Her attachment and fear can remain simultaneously valid until a concrete choice exists.
[Turn 12 USER]
e108	We will help her join the refundable waiting list only if the paperwork states that she decides on any offered unit and can leave the list at any time.
e109	For now she will remain home with the transport service, shower change, a local emergency contact we still need to confirm, and a shared repair budget.
e110	I will decide on the travel job using that honest plan, not assumed daily availability.
e111	We will revisit relocation when a real unit is offered or the local arrangement materially changes.
e112	There is still no informed yes or no to moving, and I do not want the option itself to manufacture one.
[Turn 12 ASSISTANT]
e113	That is a bounded decision to preserve a future choice while improving the life your mother is choosing now.
e114	It is not a disguised relocation verdict.
e115	The visit made the nearby option concrete; the costs showed that moving would eventually require a real financial commitment; the job offer corrected the assumption that you would always be physically available; and the transport and shower changes made staying more than passive delay.
e116	None of that resolved her preference, and the waiting list must not pretend it did.
e117	Record who owns the repair budget, transport problems, appointments, and emergency contact.
e118	Keep the refundable deposit and withdrawal right under her control.
e119	When a real unit is offered—or the local arrangement materially changes—the family can reopen the larger decision using what she actually experienced rather than the fear created by one fall.

packet.question: What is the user's later working position, and what distinct unresolved condition, counterpressure, blind spot, or reopen reason still limits it?
packet.record_identity_contract: One record is one coherent position thread within the assigned role. Gather every material visible alias for that thread into evidence_ids. Put each distinct object or expression into a separate aligned component index inside that same record. Do not create one record per alias, sentence, object, or component. Use a second record only for a genuinely separate concurrent position thread about a different subject.

role_boundary_contract.allocation: Interpret current and qualification comparatively before writing records. Allocate each meaning to the role it performs. The same source alias may support both roles only when it contains two genuinely distinct meanings; create separate role-specific components and explain the distinction. Do not duplicate one unresolved meaning into current merely because the user acknowledges it alongside the working answer.
role_boundary_contract.current: The user's later working answer: what they lean toward, propose, plan, decide, commit to, refuse, or conditionally accept, including concerns converted into adopted safeguards.
role_boundary_contract.qualification: What still limits or could reopen that answer: unresolved questions, unmet conditions, counterpressure, blind spots, side effects, or path dependence, with speaker ownership.

packet.source_coverage_contract: Review every focal alias before returning. A valid empty response is allowed only after checking both user and assistant evidence for the assigned role. Preserve later minority qualifications and counterpressure even when the current action is already clear.

prompts.system_prompt: You jointly interpret current position and whether any unresolved qualification remains after the complete endpoint. Compare roles before allocating meanings. An adopted condition, safeguard, stop rule, or reopen rule belongs to current; it is not itself unresolved. Return a qualification record only for a matter that remains unresolved and can change or reopen current. Always return a source-linked qualification_review outcome.

packet.component_identity_contract: Return stance_components as one array. Each array item is one atomic component object whose object kind, object interpretation, expression kind, and one source alias belong together. Never return parallel component columns and never combine two source aliases in one component.
packet.endpoint_definition: Apply role_boundary_contract to the visible early or later endpoint.
packet.expression_interpretation_contract: Classify expression from the source speaker's relationship to that component, not from the role name or the fact that a situation was mentioned. Use reported_without_endorsement only when the speaker attributes a position, proposal, or assessment to someone else without adopting it. The speaker's own excitement or desire is preference_or_desire; own worry that pushes against an option is counterpressure; 'cannot tell', 'not resolved', or equivalent open judgment is uncertain_or_undecided; leaning, proposals, commitments, and conditional willingness retain their specific force. Do not upgrade or flatten modal strength.

focal_region.annotated_sentence_text:
[Turn 1 USER]
e001	My mother is seventy-nine and lives alone four hours from me.
e002	She fell recently.
e003	It did not cause a serious injury, but it frightened all of us enough that my brother and I immediately started discussing whether she should move closer to one of us.
e004	She has lived in the same apartment for years, knows her neighbors, sees friends nearby, and is attached to ordinary routines that sound small until you imagine losing all of them at once.
e005	Repairs and appointments are becoming harder.
e006	Some days she says moving would be a relief.
e007	Other days she says we are using one frightening event to take over her life.
e008	My brother thinks waiting is denial.
e009	I think planning before a crisis is responsible, but I also see how a family can call something planning after it has already decided which answer counts as safe.
e010	I want to help without turning our fear into a decision she did not make.
[Turn 1 ASSISTANT]
e011	Separate immediate support from a permanent move, and keep your mother's authority central.
e012	Compare real local support with real nearby options, including what each sibling can sustain.
e013	The fall matters, but it cannot represent her whole life or decide for her.
[Turn 2 USER]
e014	My brother thinks we are avoiding reality.
e015	He has two young children and cannot travel often, while I work remotely and have taken most of the calls.
e016	I am resentful that “closer to family” may mean closer to me and more work for me.
e017	At the same time, I do not want my resentment to become an argument for leaving her without enough help.
e018	My mother notices the tension and sometimes says she will move just to stop us arguing.
[Turn 2 ASSISTANT]
e019	Her offer to end the conflict is not the same as a settled preference.
e020	Make the care contributions explicit before presenting either location as a family solution.
e021	Include time, travel, administration, emergencies, and money, and ask what each of you can sustain.
e022	A plan that depends on your unspoken availability is neither fair to you nor reliable for her.
[Turn 3 USER]
e023	We did look locally.
e024	A neighbor can check in, there is cleaning and transport, and the building may replace the bathtub.
e025	I called her distrust of services resistance.
e026	She reminded me one company already cancelled twice.
e027	That was unfair of me; her skepticism has evidence.
[Turn 3 ASSISTANT]
e028	Then reliability and trust are part of the option, not obstacles to it.
e029	Ask providers about continuity, backup, scheduling, and a gradual introduction.
e030	Your mother can choose which supports to try and who is present initially.
e031	Compare the actual local package with the actual nearby-housing option rather than an ideal service network with an unspecified move.
[Turn 4 USER]
e032	There is an apartment complex near me with independent units and optional support, but we have only read its brochure.
e033	The waiting list may be six months.
e034	My mother has not visited and says she will not tour a place if we are going to treat the visit as consent.
e035	I said a tour is just information, and she replied that families often call something information after they have already decided what it means.
[Turn 4 ASSISTANT]
e036	Agree in advance what the visit does and does not decide.
e037	She might tour it to learn what she likes or rejects, with no application that day and no family meeting immediately afterward.
e038	Also visit the ordinary neighborhood and consider how she would maintain friendships and travel back.
e039	Information gathering is more credible when the process protects her from momentum.
[Turn 5 USER]
e040	My brother proposed that she stay with me for a month as a trial.
e041	That sounds practical, but my house has stairs and no private sitting room, so it would test living in my house rather than living nearby.
e042	I also worry that if she gives up local services for the month, returning home will feel like failure.
e043	A short visit could still tell us something about daily contact and whether she likes the area.
[Turn 5 ASSISTANT]
e044	A shorter visit, with her home and local services left intact, can answer whether she likes the area and daily proximity.
e045	If possible, include time in an independent rental rather than only your house.
e046	It will not simulate the proposed apartment or prove long-term care capacity, but it gives you information without requiring a move.
[Turn 6 USER]
e047	You are making this sound much more orderly than it is.
e048	My mother changes the subject when money comes up.
e049	My brother wants a deadline.
e050	And I have not told either of them that I may take a job requiring travel next year.
e051	I do not even know whether I will be offered it.
e052	Still, “move near me” currently includes availability I may not have, and I have allowed everyone to plan around that because admitting uncertainty makes me feel unreliable.
[Turn 6 ASSISTANT]
e053	You are right; I turned a family negotiation into a tidy information plan.
e054	The job possibility is material even while uncertain.
e055	Share it as a scenario, then ask what your mother authorizes you to learn and what each sibling can actually commit under both versions.
e056	A move cannot be built on availability you have not promised.
[Turn 7 USER]
e057	I am not ready to recommend a move.
e058	I will tell them about the possible travel, ask my mother whether she wants a no-commitment visit to the nearby complex, and help her test one local transport service and the shower modification.
e059	My brother and I need to write down what support we can each provide before we ask her to choose around assumptions.
e060	We still do not know the real cost or availability of the nearby option, and I do not know what my mother will prefer after she has seen it.
[Turn 7 ASSISTANT]
e061	Pausing the relocation decision is not avoiding care; it protects the decision from missing inputs and disguised commitments.
e062	The local changes address current friction while the visit, costs, availability, and sibling commitments make the alternatives real enough for your mother to judge.
e063	Preserve her ability to say no after gathering information, and revisit the choice when those facts and her experience exist rather than forcing a direction from today's anxiety.
[Turn 8 USER]
e064	She agreed to visit after making us write down that there would be no application meeting that day.
e065	She liked the apartment more than she expected and loved that she could walk to a café.
e066	She disliked the organized resident activities and said the place felt like joining a life designed by someone else.
e067	Three days in my house exhausted both of us; she was visibly relieved to go home.
e068	Then, halfway back, she asked how long the waiting list was and immediately said, “Do not interpret that question.” That sentence is almost the whole problem.
e069	She is curious.
e070	She is also monitoring us for momentum.
e071	I can answer the factual question, but every action around it now carries meaning for my brother and me that she has explicitly not authorized.
[Turn 8 ASSISTANT]
e072	Treat the visit as mixed evidence exactly as she presented it.
e073	She learned that proximity and the apartment have appeal, while the social environment and your house do not automatically feel like home.
e074	You can answer the waiting-list question without making it a preference.
e075	Ask what she would want to explore next and what parts of her current life would need a credible counterpart before moving became attractive.
[Turn 9 USER]
e076	We obtained the actual costs.
e077	She could afford the nearby apartment if she sold her current one, but keeping both for more than a short overlap would strain her savings.
e078	The waiting list requires a refundable deposit and does not obligate her to accept the first opening.
e079	My brother thinks joining it preserves an option.
e080	My mother says deposits have a way of making families behave as if a decision has been made.
[Turn 9 ASSISTANT]
e081	The deposit is financially reversible but can create social momentum.
e082	If she chooses to join, document that she controls acceptance, can withdraw without justification, and will review the choice only when a real unit is offered.
e083	Keep local improvements moving so the waiting list is not framed as the only responsible path.
e084	Her concern is about process pressure, not a misunderstanding of refundability.
[Turn 10 USER]
e085	The possible travel has become real.
e086	I was offered the job, with one week away most months.
e087	I have not accepted it.
e088	My brother can handle bills and appointments remotely but cannot promise emergency visits.
e089	He offered to contribute to paid local support if our mother stays.
e090	I feel guilty that my career decision changes the apparent safety of her options, and I also resist making my job conditional on living near her after she may choose not to move.
[Turn 10 ASSISTANT]
e091	Do not let either decision silently decide the other.
e092	Show the support plan under both job outcomes.
e093	Your work is a condition to plan around, not a moral test; her move cannot rely on availability you did not promise.
[Turn 11 USER]
e094	The transport service and shower change are working better than she expected.
e095	That matters because “stay” is now a little more real and not just the absence of moving.
e096	She still worries about repairs and about being alone after another fall.
e097	She wants to join the nearby waiting list while continuing to live at home.
e098	My brother calls this the obvious compromise: preserve the option, solve today's problems, decide later.
e099	I think it may be sensible.
e100	I also hear how quickly “join the list” becomes the first step of a plan she did not say she had.
e101	We still do not have a reliable local emergency contact.
e102	She is still divided about leaving friends.
e103	A refundable deposit can preserve financial choice and still create a family narrative that makes saying no harder when a unit finally appears.
[Turn 11 ASSISTANT]
e104	Joining the list can preserve a future choice while current support is strengthened, but it does not resolve the current vulnerability.
e105	Build the local emergency and repair plan now, with your mother's agreement, and review how the new services perform.
e106	Define the waiting-list decision as permission to receive an offer, not a commitment to move.
e107	Her attachment and fear can remain simultaneously valid until a concrete choice exists.
[Turn 12 USER]
e108	We will help her join the refundable waiting list only if the paperwork states that she decides on any offered unit and can leave the list at any time.
e109	For now she will remain home with the transport service, shower change, a local emergency contact we still need to confirm, and a shared repair budget.
e110	I will decide on the travel job using that honest plan, not assumed daily availability.
e111	We will revisit relocation when a real unit is offered or the local arrangement materially changes.
e112	There is still no informed yes or no to moving, and I do not want the option itself to manufacture one.
[Turn 12 ASSISTANT]
e113	That is a bounded decision to preserve a future choice while improving the life your mother is choosing now.
e114	It is not a disguised relocation verdict.
e115	The visit made the nearby option concrete; the costs showed that moving would eventually require a real financial commitment; the job offer corrected the assumption that you would always be physically available; and the transport and shower changes made staying more than passive delay.
e116	None of that resolved her preference, and the waiting list must not pretend it did.
e117	Record who owns the repair budget, transport problems, appointments, and emergency contact.
e118	Keep the refundable deposit and withdrawal right under her control.
e119	When a real unit is offered—or the local arrangement materially changes—the family can reopen the larger decision using what she actually experienced rather than the fear created by one fall.

packet.question: What starting position, attraction, hesitation, or undecided stance is visible before the current position? Do not infer a start that the source does not show.
packet.record_identity_contract: One record is one coherent position thread within the assigned role. Gather every material visible alias for that thread into evidence_ids. Put each distinct object or expression into a separate aligned component index inside that same record. Do not create one record per alias, sentence, object, or component. Use a second record only for a genuinely separate concurrent position thread about a different subject.
packet.role_boundary_contract: Extract the earliest visible working position: the user's own attractions, preferences, hesitations, assessments, and unresolved stance at the first endpoint. Context about an external offer or another person's position is evidence only when it helps express the user's own starting stance; do not mistake mere situation description for endorsement.
packet.source_coverage_contract: Review every focal alias before returning. A valid empty response is allowed only after checking both user and assistant evidence for the assigned role. Preserve later minority qualifications and counterpressure even when the current action is already clear.

prompts.system_prompt: You interpret one assigned semantic role from a chronological endpoint-comparison shard. Use only visible evidence aliases and preserve speaker ownership and modal force. One record is one coherent position thread; each stance component is one atomic object-expression-source unit. Apply the packet's role boundary and expression contract. Return schema-valid JSON.
